key_insight: This paper shows that a unified multimodal model can improve both visual understanding and image generation without human labels or external reward models. It does this by making the model teach itself through internal question generation, answering, and self-consistency rewards.
problem_solved: Most unified large multimodal models depend on expensive curated supervision, such as human annotations, preference labels, or separate reward models. The paper tackles the challenge of learning stronger understanding and generation skills autonomously from only unlabeled images.
method: Use a self-evolving training loop with three internal roles: a Proposer, a Solver, and a Generator.
The Proposer creates visual questions, the Solver answers them and checks consistency, and the Generator supports image generation improvements.
Train with self-consistency rewards so the model can refine itself using only unlabeled image data.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests a path to reducing dependence on costly annotation pipelines and reward modeling. It could make multimodal systems easier to scale, cheaper to adapt, and more self-improving across both understanding and generation tasks.

paper_title: Ask, Solve, Generate: Self-Evolving Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation via Self-Consistency Rewards
paper_authors: Ritesh Thawkar, Shravan Venkatraman, Omkar Thawakar, Abdelrahman Shaker, Fahad Khan
